hypothesis: Balanced same-piece checking/nonchecking supervision can teach a local causal LLM check discrimination better than constant false.

source.license: CC0-1.0; retained prior acquisition; no new download

training: Native Qwen3-0.6B fresh r16 LoRA, full-vocabulary CE for one true/false next token; BF16 frozen base and FP32 adapter; gradient norm1; fixed seed; warmup32. No EOS/JSON generation claim.
selection: Highest development raw full-vocabulary-token correctness; then both moves of each pair correct; then earliest step including baseline. Freeze selection before holdout.
inputs: Current pre-move FEN, selected legal UCI move and occupied-square map only. No SAN/check suffix, post-move board, attacks-after, solution, theme, engine PV or target label.
evaluation: Raw unrestricted next-token argmax. Non-boolean tokens invalid, never rescued by binary renormalization. Conditional binary probabilities retained separately. Every planned example remains denominator.
exclusions: Pinned all-known history registry plus latest matched-check source games/current/before/successor boards. One new original game per pair; hash split by original game; no source solution tails consumed.
limits: Only check detection; not broad chess understanding, strategic commentary, move strength or Elo.
Selected tactical same-piece pairs; not natural-game prevalence or complete special-move coverage.
Unknown overlap with original base pretraining. Historical evaluations remain spent.
Synthetic software tests are not evidence of learned chess capability.
